selection_criteria: Exact match of the lecture topic to the knowledge node
Completeness of the necessary explanation without unrelated chapters
Clarity and accessibility appropriate to the concept
Continuity of selected course within adjacent knowledge areas
Avoid redundant teacher alternatives, broad all-in-one videos and unnecessarily advanced add-ons

selection_audit.source_selection_pool: Existing curated Bilibili video sources and their published course part listings

rationale_by_node.proof_direct_contradiction: Two individually targeted proof videos instead of an MIT introduction covering other material.
rationale_by_node.number_prime: Direct short lessons on both divisibility and primes rather than a broad Number Theory I lecture.
rationale_by_node.number_gcd: Covers exactly greatest common divisors and Euclid's algorithm.
rationale_by_node.number_congruence: Modular arithmetic is a direct lesson, rather than first portion of MIT Number Theory II.
rationale_by_node.number_linear_congruence: Specifically teaches linear congruences, while MIT Lecture 5 primarily builds toward Euler, Fermat and RSA.
rationale_by_node.count_basic: Direct counting-rules lesson, followed naturally in the same course by permutations and the binomial theorem.
rationale_by_node.proof_strong_induction: The MIT official lesson is explicitly titled Strong Induction; CMU P3 has a broader advanced-induction scope.
rationale_by_node.count_binomial: The BU lesson explicitly teaches the binomial theorem; CMU P8-9 covers coefficients and advanced Lucas theorem.
rationale_by_node.count_generating: One coherent teacher; definitions and computations followed by core counting applications, excluding advanced redundant lectures.
rationale_by_node.recurrence_model: Only the BU lesson explicitly covers modeling with recurrence relations; CMU P11 starts with linear-algebra applications.
rationale_by_node.recurrence_homogeneous: Focused linear recurrences and characteristic equations, without the generic MIT Lecture 15 duplicate.
rationale_by_node.graph_basic: Brief modular definition, subgraph, degree and regular-graph lessons rather than CMU's broad introductory graph lecture.
rationale_by_node.graph_connectivity: Theoretical and algorithmic connectedness with a directed connectivity unit; avoid redundant advanced P40-41 subroutines and mixed-topic CMU P19.
rationale_by_node.graph_euler: Dedicated Euler graph theory and construction algorithm instead of CMU's mixed connectivity-Euler lecture.
rationale_by_node.graph_hamilton: Direct Hamiltonian graph topic, rather than the traveling-salesperson application lecture.
rationale_by_node.graph_coloring: Point and edge coloring through planar coloring and theorems; CMU P32 overlaps with planar graph node.
rationale_by_node.graph_planar: Planar graphs and Euler's formula without dragging in the mixed nonplanar/Hamiltonian/coloring P44 and duplicate CMU lecture.
rationale_by_node.graph_bipartite: Dedicated bipartite graph theory; CMU P24-25 instead centers on matching.
rationale_by_node.graph_topological: Animation specifically illustrates topological sorting rather than a broader partial-order lecture.
rationale_by_node.graph_matching: Dedicated matching theory, Hungarian maximum matching and perfect matching; omit advanced Hopcroft-Karp and blossom algorithm videos.
rationale_by_node.tree_basic: Dedicated introductory tree lectures, not CMU's mixed tree-and-spanning-tree lecture.
rationale_by_node.tree_spanning: Direct spanning-tree lecture; CMU P22 teaches Cayley counting, which is a different objective.
rationale_by_node.count_pigeonhole: P6 teaches the core pigeonhole principle; P7 is advanced Diophantine approximation.
rationale_by_node.graph_weighted: Weighted-graph definition and distances, not the shortest-path algorithm taught elsewhere.
rationale_by_node.graph_cut: Cut vertices/edges theory and algorithms; cutsets/connectivity P21 is not central to the node title.
rationale_by_node.relation_property: Five lectures directly about relation properties; omitted P58 on counting special relations.

selection_audit.scope_limitation: Evaluated public syllabi, indexed video part names and available lecture descriptions/transcripts. These edits do not certify the teaching quality of every minute of every video; the live Bilibili playback status was not exhaustively checked.
